description:
FILED s439 (Fable) from s438 ask 7 -- two probe-found PRE-EXISTING shapes (Opus
verified them unchanged by Q4 on a worktree) plus the strictly-single bareword
branch's ternary miss.  RULED: one task, not two, and it belongs WITH #266 (a
bare NAME is a CALL only where it is CALLABLE; the two negatives differ) --
all three are "what does a bare WORD mean in OPERAND position" at sites #266
has not reached, which is also where #481/#482 point.

  sub fh (*) { "fh(@_)" }    print fh FOO;          # perl: fh(FOO)   PCL: (pl-fh FOO) -> unbound variable FOO, crash
  sub one ($) { "one(@_)" }  print one BAR;         # perl: one(BAR)  PCL: (pl-one (pl-BAR)) -> undefined sub
  open(G, ...);  print close G ? "a" : "b";         # perl: close(G) ? "a" : "b"   PCL: close(G ? "a" : "b")

perl: a bareword in a `(*)` slot is the handle/class NAME as a string; in a `($)`
slot under no strict it is the string "BAR" (strict subs would die -- PCL need
not detect that, principle 9); and the strictly-single bareword branch must end
at `?` as it ends at `,` and end-of-run.

DO NOT patch the `(*)` site alone: an unbound-symbol crash is at least loud, and
a per-site string answer would be the fourth copy of the classifier (#266,
#481, #482 are the others).  Find the ONE operand-position reading of a bare
Word (PExpr handle_subcalls' strictly-single branch + `_term_extent`'s bare-word
decline -- the walker declines bare words BY DESIGN, see pexpr-term-parsing-
review.md) and answer there.  `_bareword_callable_here` is the classifier.

BAR: probes (the three lines + the inverses: `one 1`, `fh $fh`, `fh STDOUT`,
`close G, 1`), guard rows in Pl/t/user-unary-01.t, corpus-diff + 951-file A/B
(every DIFF explained), gate-SET scan if a classifier answer WIDENS (s372 row).


PROGRESS s443f (Opus, agent F round 4), commit 4c32128, ff-merged s444: shapes (a) + (c) DONE.  (a) ONE helper Pl::PExpr::_read_star_slot_bareword (paren-less AND paren sites), reading the * slot's two halves apart as perl does: a BUILTIN handle slot takes the bareword as the handle even when a sub of that name is declared (sub FILE1(){42}; tell FILE1 = -1, comp/parser.t:540); a USER (*) sub CALLS a declared name, else the NAME arrives as a plain string.  (c) the strictly-single operand ends where PRECEDENCE says -- the site now calls _extend_high_prec (the named-unary helper) clamped to the #343 ceiling; close G ? "a" : "b" fixed, close G . "x" (= close("Gx")) preserved.  Fable re-probed both -- identical to perl.  REMAINS: shape (b) `sub one ($); print one BAR` -- the two ALL-CAPS escapes in handle_subcalls (~3922, ~4352) are LOAD-BEARING (an imported constant the export scan cannot see must stay a funcall; probed: widening regresses Foo::BAR).  This is #266's ruled asymmetry -- fix belongs with the #266 classifier, not per-site.
subject: A BAREWORD operand of a prototyped user sub: `fh FOO` with `(*)` emits an UNBOUND CL symbol (crash), `one BAR` with `($)` a CALL to an undeclared sub, and `close G ? "a" : "b"` parses as `close(G ? ...)` -- perl gives the string / the ternary (ask 7 of s438, ruled s439: ONE task, in #266's family)
